subject: Emotions
title: Surprise vs Startle
description: A micro-lesson that makes Surprise vs Startle usable.

hook.text: A car backfires. You flinch before you think. That's startle—a reflex, not an emotion.

buildup.text: Startle is hardwired in the brainstem and takes 30 milliseconds. Surprise is processed in the cortex.

discovery.text: You can habituate to startle: soldiers stop flinching at gunfire. But surprise never habituates.

twist.text: Horror movies exploit the confusion. Jump scares trigger startle, but the brain labels it as surprise.

climax.text: Startle protects you from danger. Surprise protects you from being wrong about the world.

punchline.text: Startle is your body reacting. Surprise is your mind updating.

quiz.question: Where is the startle reflex processed?
